title: Inventory screen (grouped, filterable, searchable) + item detail with plain-language prediction explanation
goal: Give the household a screen that turns item_stats + v_current_stock into an at-a-glance, filterable view of what's in stock and what needs attention, plus a per-item drill-down that explains the prediction in plain language -- the first UI surface for E-5's prediction output.
in_scope: lib/inventory/data.ts: getInventoryItems(householdId) -> batched fetch of catalog_items (household, is_archived=false) joined with v_current_stock (raw qty_base), item_stats (predicted_depletion_at, predicted_next_purchase_at, daily_rate_base, rate_correction, cadence_bucket, confidence, last_purchased_at), and categories (name, slug), plus a trailing-90d avg unit_price and last-8-points price series per item from price_history -- batched (one query per table, not per-item N+1), matching lib/predictions/recompute.ts's recomputeAllItemsForHousehold() batching precedent.

lib/inventory/virtualStock.ts: pure function computeVirtualStockBase({ rawStockBase, dailyRateBase, rateCorrection, predictedDepletionAt, now }) -> number, implementing F9.2's 'decremented virtually for display and prediction using daily_rate_base.' Derives from the SAME predicted_depletion_at / daily_rate_base item_stats already persists (no new persisted field): dailyRate = dailyRateBase * rateCorrection; daysRemaining = (predictedDepletionAt - now) in days; virtualStock = max(0, dailyRate * daysRemaining). Falls back to raw stock when dailyRateBase or predictedDepletionAt is null (no rate signal yet, e.g. q<0.70 or first purchase) -- nothing to project, so raw ledger truth is the honest answer. Shared by S-20's consumption UI and the Today stub addition.

app/inventory/page.tsx (server component): grouped-by-category list with 'Out of stock' and 'Running low' pinned above the grouped list (F8); category / cadence-bucket / stock-state / staples-only filters plus free-text search-across-name-and-aliases, all via URL searchParams (server-rendered filtering, no client state library -- matches this repo's existing pattern of no client data-fetching library beyond react-query already in package.json but unused so far). Item card shows: current stock (virtual, base + friendly display e.g. '1.5 kg ≈ 3 packs'), predicted days remaining (from predicted_next_purchase_at -- see invariants for why not predicted_depletion_at), cadence badge, last purchased, avg price (90d), trend sparkline (inline SVG, no charting dependency, price_history points).

app/inventory/[id]/page.tsx: item detail -- purchase history timeline (stock_movements for the item, all types), price chart (price_history, same inline-SVG approach as the card sparkline, more points), and a plain-language prediction explanation string assembled from item_stats fields (e.g. 'You buy this every ~9 days; last bought 7 days ago; ~2 days left').

A narrow base-unit -> friendly-display formatter (e.g. 1500g -> '1.5 kg', with an approx-packs suffix when default_pack_size is set) -- the inverse direction of S-10's normalizeUnitToBase, kept as its own small function rather than a generalized inverse of that whole module.
out_of_scope: Cadence override / mark staple / set perishability / archive controls -- the working spec's F8 paragraph lists these on item detail, but they are catalog-management actions owned by E-11's S-30 (merge/archive/recategorize) and E-8's S-21 (Plan screen cadence override with revert-to-auto). Building them here would create a second owner for the same state. This screen is read + explain only.

Persisting item_stats.avg_unit_price_90d -- that column exists in the schema but no story has ever written it. S-19 computes the 90-day average at read time from price_history rather than reaching into computeItemStats/recompute.ts (E-5 territory) to start writing it.
Any change to computeItemStats, recompute.ts, reconcile.ts, or any item_stats write path -- this story is read-only against existing E-4/E-5 output.
acceptance: Item card shows current stock, predicted days remaining, cadence badge, last purchased, avg price, trend sparkline.
invariants: Current stock displayed on the card and detail is the VIRTUAL projection (F9.2, computeVirtualStockBase), never a raw v_current_stock passthrough -- the two are equal only at the instant of the item's last recompute and diverge as real time passes between recomputes, by design (this is what makes the app 'look right' for a household that logs nothing).

virtualStock never exceeds raw v_current_stock: at recompute time, dailyRate * (predictedDepletionAt - now) == dailyRate * (rawStock / dailyRate) == rawStock exactly, by construction of predicted_depletion_at in computeItemStats; it can only be equal or lower after that, never higher. Worth a direct hand-fixture check, not just an assertion.

'Predicted days remaining' is read from predicted_next_purchase_at, not predicted_depletion_at -- the latter is null whenever the rate-cross-check's q<0.70 gate isn't met (e.g. any item with even one qty_base=null purchase in its trailing window), while predicted_next_purchase_at is populated for every item with >=1 purchase (blendNextPurchase falls back to the interval-based estimate when the rate signal is absent). Using predicted_depletion_at here would blank the field for a large share of real items.
No write path anywhere in this story -- purely additive read-only screens on top of E-4/E-5's existing data.
